figures.caption: Figure 1: Overview of DAER for continual Video-MLLM adaptation over evolving domains. DAER routes inputs from sequentially arriving video domains to domain-specific expert pools. Moreover similar domains can be adaptively merged for improved parameter efficiency.
Figure 3: Results under the 20-task continual learning setting. Each original domain is further divided into two sequential sub-tasks, yielding a 20-task stream.
Figure 4: Ablation study on four important components.
Figure 5: Sensitivity study on four critical hyper-parameters.
Table 6: Detailed Component Analysis of DAER.
Figure 7: Qualitative comparison between DAM and the proposed DAER on representative VidQA examples.

Figure 2: Illustration of the DAER framework for continual Video-MLLM adaptation over evolving domains. DAER performs inter-domain routing to identify the most relevant domain, intra-domain routing to activate domain-specific experts and adaptive domain merging to reduce redundancy across similar domains.
